findings.what: Says "For each email, Substack shows us how many readers opened it and clicked its links". That reads as aggregate counts only. Substack's own help pages say the publisher also sees each subscriber's own open counts ("Email opens (last 7 days, 30 days, 6 months)", "Emails opened (last 6 months)") and, on opening a subscriber's record, "recent activity (emails received, emails opened, link clicks)". A reader who relies on this page would believe individual opens and clicks are not visible to the publisher, and they are. The next clause (an activity rating per subscriber) hints at it but does not say it.
findings.evidence: https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/360058529871-How-do-I-use-the-subscriber-dashboard-on-Substack (columns list, fetched via the help-center API 2026-11-06); https://on.substack.com/p/subscriber-dashboard-guide ("Clicking an individual subscriber's email shows recent activity (emails received, emails opened, link clicks)"); https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/6461334789652 (stars = activity from email opens and web views)
findings.fix: Say it per person: "Substack shows us, for each subscriber, how many of our emails they opened and which links they clicked, and gives each an activity rating based on email opens and web views."

findings.where: site/privacy.md, section "This site", last sentence, and "Your choices" (Do Not Track bullet)
findings.what: "lets no other party collect information about what you do here" and "this site ... track[s] no one" sit one sentence after the page says GitHub logs every visitor's IP address. The host necessarily sees which pages are requested, so the sentences overreach as written. The IP-logging sentence itself is accurate (GitHub Docs, Data collection: "the visitor's IP address is logged and stored for security purposes, regardless of whether the visitor has signed into GitHub or not").
findings.fix: "The site itself sets no cookies and runs no analytics or tracking scripts, and it loads nothing from other parties." Only keep the last clause if the built site really loads nothing third-party (not checked here). In the Do Not Track bullet say "the site runs no tracking of its own".

findings.where: site/privacy.md, "The newsletter" paragraph 2 and "Who gets your information"; compare welcome/paid.md "Your membership renews..."
findings.what: Says "If you buy a paid subscription, Stripe processes the payment and holds your card details" and that only Substack, Stripe and the AI service get your information. paid.md itself says some readers subscribe in Substack's iPhone app, where Apple's in-app payment system takes the payment (Substack: "readers pay Apple"). For those readers Apple, not Stripe, handles the card. Substack's privacy policy also lists "credit card details" among data Substack collects, with Stripe as its processor, so "Stripe ... holds" is more specific than the source.
findings.evidence: https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/19718129670420-Can-my-subscribers-pay-on-the-Substack-iOS-app ; https://substack.com/privacy ("we use Stripe (a third party payment provider) to receive and process your credit card transactions for us"; "payment details (including billing address, credit card details...)")
findings.fix: "If you buy a paid subscription, Substack's payment processor, Stripe, handles the card (or Apple does, if you subscribe in Substack's iPhone app); we never see your card number." Add Apple to "Who gets your information" or say "and the payment processor you choose".

findings.where: welcome/paid.md, HTML comment at top (and the paste instructions)
findings.what: Tells the publisher to paste this into "Welcome email (paid)" once founding memberships go on sale January 5, 2027. Substack has a separate "Welcome email to founding subscribers" template: "If you have payments enabled and a reader subscribes as a founding member, they'll receive this email." The first buyers (founding members) would therefore get Substack's default text, not this email, unless it is pasted into the founding template too.
findings.evidence: https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/24034796625428-How-do-I-set-up-welcome-emails-on-Substack (four welcome templates: free, paid, imported, founding)
findings.fix: Add to the comment: "Paste it into 'Welcome email to founding subscribers' as well."

findings.where: welcome/paid.md, "What doesn't change", sentence "Your membership renews automatically each year until you cancel."
findings.what: True only for an annual plan. Substack subscriptions also come in monthly intervals (Substack dashboard: "subscription intervals like monthly or annual"). I could not see from the pieces which plans will be sold; if a monthly plan exists, a monthly subscriber would be told the wrong renewal period.
findings.fix: If only annual plans are sold, keep it. Otherwise: "Your membership renews automatically at the end of each billing period (a month or a year, whichever you chose) until you cancel."

findings.where: welcome/free.md ("each comes with a free calculator"), welcome/start-here.md ("each comes with a free calculator"), welcome/about.md ("links to a free calculator")
findings.what: Says every answer comes with a free calculator. schedule.json issue 13 (2027-03-30) says outright "There's no new calculator" (its tool is "Every Q1 model, for paying members"), and issues 26, 46, 51 and 35/52 list a survey page, an interactive report, a preview and reader questions rather than a calculator. A reader would expect a calculator every Tuesday and not get one on those weeks.
findings.fix: "most issues come with a free calculator" (or "each comes with a free tool").
